name: Tests
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
jobs:
  test-core:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - name: Setup Keyring
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y gnome-keyring
          echo 'somecredstorepass' | gnome-keyring-daemon --unlock
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@f10502fc09dadecfefb962fff68ce77213930204 # v4
      - name: Core Tests
        env:
          GO_TEST_PARALLEL: "16"
        run: mise run test:ci:core

  test-integration:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [a, b, c]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - name: Setup Keyring
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y gnome-keyring
          echo 'somecredstorepass' | gnome-keyring-daemon --unlock
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@f10502fc09dadecfefb962fff68ce77213930204 # v4
      - name: Integration Tests
        env:
          GO_TEST_PARALLEL: "16"
        run: mise run test:ci:integration:shard -- ${{ matrix.shard }}

  test-canary:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # Run the (no-cost, no-API) Vogon canary against each checkpoint backend so
      # the git-refs store is guarded on every PR alongside the default git-branch.
      matrix:
        checkpoint_store: [git-branch, git-refs]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - name: Setup Keyring
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y gnome-keyring
          echo 'somecredstorepass' | gnome-keyring-daemon --unlock
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@f10502fc09dadecfefb962fff68ce77213930204 # v4
      - name: E2E Canary
        env:
          E2E_CHECKPOINT_STORE: ${{ matrix.checkpoint_store }}
        run: mise run test:e2e:canary

  test-windows:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      # Real-Windows tests must include Windows or MSYS in their top-level
      # test name so this job selects them without running POSIX-only harnesses.
      - name: Windows unit tests
        run: go test ./cmd/entire/cli/... -run '(Windows|MSYS)' -count=1 -v

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs:
      - test-core
      - test-integration
      - test-canary

Found it. Here's what's actually happening:

## The hang is `apt-get update`, not the keyring

Every ubuntu job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` starts with a `Setup Keyring` step that runs `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y gnome-keyring`. Log from a job that hung this morning (`test-integration (a)`, run 32237694402):

```
09:28:04 Ign:2 http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu noble InRelease      ← retried 3x
09:28:10 Hit:2 https://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu noble InRelease           ← mirror fallback
09:28:11 Get:5 https://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu noble-security InRelease [126 kB]
15:28:09 ##[error]The operation was canceled.                              ← 6h later
```

The Azure Ubuntu mirror stops answering, apt falls back to `archive.ubuntu.com` via the mirrorlist, and that connection stalls mid-download without apt ever timing out. In a healthy run the same step is `Hit:2 http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com...` and finishes in ~15s.

Two things make it as painful as you experienced:

1. **It's per-runner, not per-run** — on your current PR, `test-canary (git-refs)` got through in 3m27s while five sibling jobs are stuck 25 min and counting. So a rerun is a dice roll, not a fix.
2. **The ubuntu jobs have no `timeout-minutes`**, so a stuck one burns the default **360-minute** timeout before GitHub kills it. That's the "took a really long time or needed a cancel" part. It's not new either — I found jobs hung 02:52→08:53 and 09:02→15:03 today, all exactly 6h.

## The step is dead weight

It was added in `8f6242a43` (Mar 14) when the auth store talked straight to the OS keyring. That's no longer true: `tokenstore.resolveBackendLocked` returns a temp `fileStore` under `go test` via `internal/testdirs`, and every TestMain that spawns the real binary (`cmd/entire/cli/global_test.go`, `integration_test/setup_test.go`, `e2e/tests/main_test.go`) sets `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file` process-wide. Nothing in these jobs can reach a Secret Service — and even if it did, `callKeyringWithTimeout` bounds the call. The daemon line is inert too: it prints `SSH_AUTH_SOCK=...` and never reaches `$GITHUB_ENV`.

So the whole step exists to make three PR-blocking jobs depend on an Ubuntu mirror.

## What I changed (local only, on `soph/setup-keyring`)

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`: dropped all three `Setup Keyring` steps — that removes apt from the PR path entirely — and added `timeout-minutes: 30` to `test-core`, `test-integration`, and `test-canary`, so any future hang fails in 30 min instead of 6 hours (those jobs normally run 2–8 min; worst recent shard was 21 min). Header comment records why, so it doesn't get re-added. YAML parses; no Go code touched.

Not touched: `e2e.yml`, `e2e-checkpoint-store.yml`, `e2e-checkpoints-v2.yml` still `apt-get install gnome-keyring tmux`. They genuinely need `tmux`, so removing the keyring half doesn't remove their apt dependency, and they already carry 40-minute job timeouts. Worth a follow-up, not part of this fix.

Want me to push this and open a PR? And separately — the six stuck jobs on #2056 will sit there until ~23:00 UTC on their own; say the word and I'll cancel the run so it can be rerun against a merged fix.

git add .github/workflows/ci.yml && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
ci: drop the apt-installed keyring from the Linux test jobs

Every ubuntu job in the Tests workflow began with `apt-get update &&
apt-get install -y gnome-keyring`. When the Azure Ubuntu mirror stops
answering, apt falls back to archive.ubuntu.com via the mirrorlist and
stalls mid-download without ever timing out, so the step hangs. With no
timeout-minutes on these jobs, the hang runs to the default 360-minute
job timeout before GitHub kills it. It hits individual runners, not
whole runs — on one PR a canary job cleared the step in 3m27s while five
siblings hung — so rerunning is a dice roll rather than a fix.

The step has been dead weight since the token store stopped talking
straight to the OS keyring. resolveBackendLocked returns a temp fileStore
under `go test` via internal/testdirs, and every TestMain that spawns the
real binary sets ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file process-wide, so nothing in
these jobs can reach a Secret Service; callKeyringWithTimeout would bound
the call even if something did. The daemon line was inert too: it prints
SSH_AUTH_SOCK to stdout, which never reaches $GITHUB_ENV.

Removing it takes apt off the PR-blocking path entirely. timeout-minutes:
30 on the three ubuntu jobs caps any future hang well above their normal
2-8m (worst recent shard: 21m) and far below 6h.

The e2e workflows still install gnome-keyring alongside tmux. They need
tmux regardless, so dropping the keyring half would not remove their apt
dependency, and they already carry 40-minute job timeouts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
